title: MV (FIXED) Adventure through The Vortex of Valor -  A classic-format RPG

posts.author: Pixelbird14
posts.body:
Synopsis:
You've woken up in a dark, mysterious cave... You see a fairy-person... THING standing at the exit of the cave, and they tell you you are this world's last hope for being saved. However, they didn't really tell you why, or how to really even do anything. You have faint memories of a past life, but none of them feel real. As you explore the world, you realize what's truly at play here: a chaotic being called The SHADOW is supposedly causing mass suffering and terrorism throughout the lands... supposedly. (What even is the name of this place?) For now, though, your best shot at figuring out how anything works is to just do what the fairy-thing says. Throughout all of this, though, you feel that... something... SOMEONE else is at play here, and is controlling you all like puppets.
Characters:
Falken: It's you... probably. Your main trait is that you are good at counterattacking, but you have the urge to be really apathetic at the same time. You have a sense of humor... or sickness. Whatever it is, you have to accept this is you now.
Corgon: A dark elf who likes two things: Punching things and eating sandwiches. He's very full of himself, and is often very trigger-happy. You're pretty sure he never went to school, since when you knock on his head, it sounds hallow. He's very optimistic, however, and often lightens the mood when things are tough.
Pyxis: She's a former student from a school that specializes in teaching magic, but the students are never allowed to leave. You managed to help her escape, but now you have both the school's superintendent and principal on your tail, chasing immortality... for some reason. Besides that, she's very snarky, and is often frank with what she says... except around Corgon, for some reason. Whatever. At least she's good at zapping things.
Slime: Literally a slime. He knows fluent English for some reason, and he likes to travel the world for the fun of it. After meeting each other a couple times, he decides to join you on your quest. He's still trying to become a good hero, and he's certainly trying his best. (He makes a good shield.) ...You feel something odd about him... Something
familiar
.
???: It's the fairy... person... thing. She refuses to tell you anything about herself. That's basically it.
This is your life now.

posts.author: TRIDIUM
posts.body:
I did this on a whim, and it's not really my usual full feedback, so I'm not going to bother posting on my main thread. Anywho, feedback a la bullet points.
Spoiler
-Default Sound effects. Unless you are on a time crunch, there's no reason to have those abominations. At least use the tick sound if you must.
-For the tutorial fight, I would suggest starting with a black screen so you don't see the battle transition.
-Music is very loud. Had to turn computer volume down to 4.
-Telling the player that there might be a button in the menu that they shouldn't press is poor design. Fix the bug.
-There were a few points where there was no music, no ambience...that can work in some games, but not in this one.
-The bestiary has like 7 trillion slots, and navigating it is difficult. Make sure you don't have extra enemy slots.
-Can walk on top of trees in multiple areas
-Forest was way to big. Lots of walking while looking at RTP tree autotiles in a straight line.
-On a light note, at this point my Uzi Shimeji decided to toss my feedback into the void. If you do not know what a Shimeji is, look it up. They're kinda fun and help me stay focused.
-Remove TP. As far as I know, it does nothing.
-THe area after the forest is painful to traverse. Random encounters every 3 steps if you're lucky, big empty rooms with nothing in them.
-Every encounter felt the same. Spam attack or the attack all enemies skill. Wait for the long animations to finish. Heal. Rinse and repeat. At the very least, add some basic elemental triangles or something.
-In the city, you can get on top of the walls by going to the top of the map. You might want to look at some basic mapping tutorials.
-Had no idea what to do in city, once again, lots of empty space with nothing in it.
-Stopped at the ghost guy fight. Not only was it weird that it switched to sideview, but he could deal more damage than you could heal. I don't believe I was underleveled, because I wandered around in the city for 20 minutes fighting every enemy and I never even got close to leveling up.
-Final note, story. Have no idea what was going on, didn't care, because the world and characters were pretty standard RPG Maker stuff so I had no desire to learn more.
I have no idea how much longer the game is, but considering I was still in Act 1 and I had 55 minutes logged (not counting me dying), I don't feel like going back and trying again.

posts.author: hiddenone
posts.body:
Heyas, I gave your game a try, but ended up giving up after getting a few game overs in the purple-tinted town. Congrats on finishing your project, but I think it could have done with more tweaking and polishing.
Spoiler:
Feedback
First thing, good job including a tutorial right at the start. A lot of games forget that explaining mechanics is an important step, so making sure that your players are equipped to win battles was a good choice. I also liked seeing another version of Falken, Corgon, and an unknown party member on another path in the forest after the minotaur, it hinted at a deeper story that I unfortunately didn't get to see.
Battles, on the other hand, really could use more love and attention. It was nice that Falken started with some skills, but I only ever used Revival once (and only outside of battle) because of how much HP and MP it takes. Corgon had no armor, and I never came across a shop or chest with armor in it, so he kept getting hit for tons of damage each turn. Falken was stuck healing him about a third of the time, unless I was able to wipe out the enemy troop quickly. Since every skill required MP and not TP, I had to save most of Falken's MP for Healing so he didn't get to use his Wild Slashes skill very often unless there were five or more enemies in a troop. Corgon also had a tendency to miss when attacking with Fury Punch. I know that's mostly due to my terrible RNG luck, but it was still a bother in battle when he'd only get one attack pretty often and that attack would miss. I ended up giving up on his skills and just going with normal attacks because the cost just wasn't worth the possible results. So for most battles I just spammed Attack and hoped for the best.
If each of them had some TP-based skills then I would have felt safer to play around and try out different strategies in battle. If Corgon had a Reckless Charge skill that cost 25 TP but could fail 25% of the time (don't actually do 25%, it would end poorly), I would have used that way more often than Fury Punch since I would be able to recover the TP later in battle. Falken could have a TP-based skill that struck one enemy twice or attack two random enemies, or have Stab use TP, would give him more options while still letting players save some of their MP for emergency healing situations.
Enemies in general felt unbalanced, each area had their own versions of the enemies and they were all stronger than the previous area, which meant that either I had to grind before moving on (since I couldn't go back to other areas) in hopes of being strong enough to survive a bunch of encounters or I had to try to avoid battles as much as possible. Since enemies could do 100 damage per turn, I never felt safe using Corgon's Rile Up skill since he usually was targeted. Each enemy's individual HP was fine, since I could defeat most in two attacks, but so many troops had 4+ enemies that by the end of the fight Corgon was almost dead and Falken had to skip attacking to keep Corgon alive. It would be an interesting twist in the game if Falken was meant to be more of a support character even though he's the 'hero', but I don't think that was quite what you're going for at the moment. If you were, then giving Falken some more support-based skills like buffs or debuffs would be a great way to show that without spelling it out with dialogue.
Mapping also suffered from being too mazelike. Most of them were built like hallways, which is a shame since you could have added a lot of extra worldbuilding details into the maps to tempt your players with hints to what else in the world is strange. Like I mentioned earlier, seeing the other version of the party in the minotaur's forest but not being able to interact or learn anything else at that moment really made it feel like there's a lot more to the story than first shown. If you gave your maps a makeover where little scenes like that could be spotted if players explored enough or section's looked like they were glitched (such as the snowy plant in the desert area, if the ground around it also included snow so it looked like a chunk of a different map was wrongly loaded in the desert map), which would make maps more interesting in general and give players another reason to look around instead of going from point A straight to point B. I think it would be good for you to scroll through the game & map feedback threads and take inspiration from some of the other maps there, you can really learn a lot by seeing how other people solve mapping problems.
As I said, I gave up in the town. The enemies just did too much damage to me to be able to explore it enough to figure out what to do, and none of the buildings seemed to do anything so I was stuck wandering aimlessly until I ran out of HP. There seemed to be something interesting in the story itself, but the gameplay just didn't engage me enough to stick through all the battles.
There were also a number of misspellings and other oddities:
Their is misspelled in most of its appearances as 'thier'
Is Willow-Whisp a joke, or did you mean "will-o'-wisp"?
Misspelled 'assaulted' as 'assulted'
Why is the snowy bush in the desert area activated by walking near it, not interacting with it?
The first forest map after the minotaur fight can't be exited by walking into the edge of the map, the player needs to hit spacebar. That doesn't match how the rest of the game works, so it feels like it could confuse players
Can't enter any of the buildings in the town
Overall, it's great that you were able to finish and release a game! But at the moment there are a lot of pieces of the game that feel rushed and unbalanced. Spending more time cleaning up your maps and balancing the battles would go a long way to improving the gameplay so people can stick around to enjoy your story.
Good luck with your future projects!

posts.author: Jorel

I did it. I beat the game. And it's possible that I am the first person ever to complete
Adventure Through the Vortex of Valor
(besides the developer), considering there was a game-breaking bug halfway through the game that nobody else caught before I had to point it out to the developer so they could fix it.
And let me tell you, it was one of the games of all time. Many laughs were shared. Many tears were shed. Many memories were created, both good and bad. The game did many things right. The game did many things wrong. Charles Dickens put it best, "It was the best of times. It was the worst of times." And as I reminisce on the journey I witnessed Falken and his companions have, I think to myself, "This truly was an adventure through the Vortex of Valor."
@Pixelbird14
, you've got yourself a new subscriber.

posts.author: Jorel
posts.body:
Pixelbird14 said:
Hey, thanks for playing and beating my game! (You're acting like this is art.)
Click to expand...
That's because it is art. You obviously spent a lot of time on this game, and it shows. I think that makes it worthy to be called art.
Anyway, sorry for the wait. I've been compiling all my thoughts and critiques for you. This is all just my own personal opinions, so take them with grains of salt if you want to, because I can't speak for every gamer ever.
Spoiler
- First of all, I'd like to point out that this RPG is a lot different from others I've played due to the fact that you can't return to any map you leave from (unless you return there during the story). I like to describe it as an "RPG on rails". This isn't necessarily a bad thing, but I do have a couple problems with it.
Grinding. If you exit a map with enemy encounters to a map with no enemy encounters, you won't be able to return to the previous map to grind levels if you get stuck during a tough boss battle.
Items. There are only a handful of opportunities during the story where you are able to buy items. I always felt like I needed to spend all my money on items whenever I could because I had no idea when I would be able to buy more.
- I think the enemy random encounter rate was too high. It felt like you couldn't go 10 steps without triggering a battle. Battles also got very tedious and unrewarding after a while, and I found myself running from most battles when I could late into the game.
- Some dungeons are way too big. The most notable for me were the ice cave and the forest after the city. The ice cave was like four huge mazes in a row, which got tiring after a while. And the forest. At the end of the forest, I didn't answer the skeleton's question correctly the first time, so I got a game over. Imagine if I hadn't saved at all since the beginning of the forest? I would have had to spend another hour navigating and fighting enemies just to get back to where I was. On that note:
- Put yourself in the players shoes. You want your player to enjoy your game, so don't give them reasons not to. I felt I had to save every chance I got because I never knew when I might get an unfair game over. Another example is the treasure chest tease on the never-ending road. Maybe it's a pretty funny joke to you, but it wasn't that funny for me.
- I had trouble figuring out where to go in some places. During the blimp ride, I didn't realize I had to actually disembark from the blimp before I could go to the next area. I eventually figured out how. In the city, I wandered around for about 45 minutes interacting with everything until I finally found an item shop that I was supposed to go into. Looking back on that, that could have just been me being dumb, but still! Make sure directions are clear.
- Some gameplay elements were a miss for me.
Reviving party members never felt worthwhile since most items only revive them with 1 HP and the revive spells, never mind being nearly impossible to use, end up leaving you in a worse spot than you were before because they require nearly all your HP and MP,
Personally, I'm not a fan of spells that use a percentage of MP. What's the point of levelling up to get more MP if a spell always uses 50% of your Max MP anyway? I'm thankful you included MP regeneration in your game for this reason.
Later in the game you get weapons that require you to time your attacks by stopping the bar in the middle of a power gauge, which really messed me up. There's no indication of when it's about to happen and as soon as I realize it's on the screen it's already gone. The only time it worked was during the last phase of the final battle where Falken was the only character in the party, so I always knew when it was going to happen.
- The balance feels off in some places. The shadow sector bosses are a big problem here. The first boss of the Shadow Sector feels a LOT more difficult compared to the rest of the shadow bosses for your team's power at the beginning of the game. That boss battle is going to be what makes most of your players turn your game off. The rest of the shadow sector bosses for me seemed to get relatively easier throughout the game.
- I was confused about whether you could actually choose your own path in the game. I thought I would be able to betray the Sovereign by acting against his wishes, but I realized I never had a choice to begin with.
- Save your credits for the end. It's really cool that you're collaborating with all these other developers, but I wouldn't give them a shoutout during the middle of your game. You want your player to be immersed in the story and doing that could break their immersion. Also, be careful with your fourth wall breaks. I think some are good, but you seemed to use them liberally. There's a point in the game where the Sovereign doesn't want your team to learn that they are in a video game, but it's clear through some dialogue that the characters already know. Like, Pyxis says, "I hope whoever designed this forest level will die alone in a dumpster" or something along those lines. By the way, don't be so hard on yourself.
Despite everything I said, I really did enjoy your game. I really liked all your characters, and the game's humor got a laugh out of me on several occasions. Boss battles were challenging and fun most of the time, and the final battle and post-game battles were a fulfilling test of strength and strategy. Can't wait to see how your game-development skills improve for the sequel.

1. I'm glad you enjoyed the bossfights! The main gameplay gimmick for this trilogy is that there are bosses EVERYWHERE. Think about it: in world like an RPG with an infinite amount of randomly appearing creatures that give you strength boosts, would there NOT be tons of super-strong foes?
2. I understand your struggles with the mazes. The main thing I had problems with during the making of the game was balancing XP and Progression, and the only way I could figure out how to evenly distribute XP without one party member leveling up faster than the rest was to increase the amounts of regular fights and give REDISTRIBUTED SOUL a higher XP rate due to how easily she would knock out.
